checks: A proper inclusion-minimal subcover of size k<j inherits linear independence, so its normal rank is k and the fixed-subcover theorem gives effective dimension k-1, including k=1 and gamma_0=1. The derivative of q log(q/(q+1)) is -log(1+1/q)+1/(q+1)<0 for q>0, and gamma_0>gamma_1. At alpha>0 the coefficient replacement increases the left side strictly, and the omitted positive parts are nonnegative.

The affine margin image is compact convex and disjoint from the open negative orthant. Weak separation in the indicated orientation gives a nonzero lambda whose supremum on the orthant is finite. Any negative coefficient would make it infinite; with lambda>=0 the supremum is zero. At any point of K, t>=0 forces at least one positively weighted margin to be nonnegative. Thus any zero coefficient would give a proper subcover, so lambda_i>0 for every i in the minimal case.

The j affine coordinates (ell_1,...,ell_{j-1},t) have independent linear parts: replacing ell_j by t multiplies the coordinate-change determinant by lambda_j>0. They extend to affine coordinates in dimension D, including j=D with no remaining coordinates. Here t is nonconstant, nonnegative on K and has null zero set, and each original margin is homogeneous linear in (v,t).

The projective marginal parent applies with r=j-1, which is in [1,D-1]. Its density is bounded and integrable, its positive set convex and full-dimensional, and its inverse power -1/j is finite positive and convex there. Restricting the density to the open positive interior discards only a null boundary and leaves all masses unchanged; the projected support itself need not be bounded.

Dividing the margins by t>0 gives z_i for i<j and (1-sum_{i<j} lambda_i z_i)/lambda_j for the last margin. All are nonconstant since j>=2 and every lambda_i>0. Their positively weighted sum is 1 on all of projective space, so some projected margin is strictly positive at every point. The open-cover parent applies with r=j-1 and beta=j; its hypotheses include the possible unbounded support and require no positivity assumption on individual cap masses.

Setting alpha=a>0 gives the strict overlap inequality because all differences A_i-a are nonnegative. It is not valid to substitute alpha=0 into a statement for alpha>0 to obtain a strict overlap. The displayed cube example has independent coordinate normals, one full cap and j-1 empty caps, so overlap is zero when a=0. The proof gives fixed-configuration strictness and no uniform gap or mixed-integer summation assertion.
